subject: Food Science
title: Physical Hazards
description: A short lesson to help you apply Physical Hazards.

hook.text: A broken tooth from a metal fragment in canned soup. Physical hazards cause injury—and lawsuits—instantly.

buildup.text: Physical hazards are foreign objects: glass, metal, bone, stones, plastic, wood, or even jewelry from food handlers.

discovery.text: Metal detectors and X-ray machines scan food production lines. They catch fragments as small as 1 mm in diameter.

twist.text: The most common physical contaminant in restaurants isn't metal or glass—it's hair. Simple caps and nets prevent it.

climax.text: A single physical hazard incident can trigger a recall of millions of units and cost a company tens of millions in damages.

punchline.text: One glass shard can ruin a brand. Detection systems run continuously for a reason.

quiz.question: What is the most common physical contaminant in restaurants?
